item.title: Medical office building in east Manatee County sells for $3.6M
item.description: A fully occupied medical office building recently sold in east Manatee County, just outside Lakewood Ranch. Sina Holdings II LLC purchased the property at 8614 State Road 70 E. for $3.6 million, according to SVN Commercial Advisory Group, which brokered the deal.The 14,400-square-foot building is within the Ranch Lake office and retail complex just east of Interstate 75. item.title: Fort Myers portfolio sells for $30 million
item.description: A New Jersey real estate investment firm has paid $30 million for an industrial flex portfolio in Fort Myers.The properties are at 6150-6481 Metro Plex Drive and total 218,000 square feet.Lee County property records show the buyer is an LLC with an address matching that of B&D Holding, a Warren, New Jersey privately held investment and development firm specializing in industrial properties. item.title: Retired attorney, family donate $10M to Naples hospital
item.description: The Coletti family in Collier County has given $10 million to Naples Comprehensive Health to advance oncology services for women at the hospital. The gift is in honor of the life and legacy of Brynne Coletti, who died in December 2024 from brain cancer at 67. NCH will recognize this gift through the naming of the Bob and Brynne Coletti Women’s Cancer Program, according to a statement. item.description: Port CharlotteDeveloper plans fast-food restaurant on retail siteAlliant Partners Development, a Tampa-based real estate development firm, has bought nearly an acre in Port Charlotte, where it is in the process of building a new restaurant on the space. item.title: Bank of America reopens Sarasota office; plans $29M investment in region
item.description: A Bank of America branch on U.S. 41 in Sarasota County has reopened following a more than yearlong closure due to renovations. item.title: Parc Center for Disabilities to open St. Petersburg location
item.description: The Tampa Bay area’s only nonprofit providing lifelong support for those with intellectual and developmental disabilities is ready to open a new campus in St. Petersburg this week. The Parc Center for Disabilities will hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony Wednesday for its new children’s services center at 3151 73rd St. N. in St. Petersburg, according to a release.
